meta.name: Jubilant Foodworks Ltd
meta.about: Jubilant FoodWorks Limited (JFL/Company) is part of the Jubilant Bhartia Group and is one of the India’s largest food service Company. The Company holds the master franchise rights for two international brands, Domino’s Pizza and Popeyes in its food segment. The Company also launched its first homegrown brand – Hong’s Kitchen in Chinese cuisine segment. [1]
meta.keyPoints: Brand Portfolio 1) Domino’s: The company is a leading player in the pizza segment, holding exclusive rights to operate Domino’s Pizza outlets in India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Nepal, Turkey, Azerbaijan, and Georgia. 2) Popeyes: It exclusively operates Popeyes in India. Popeyes is the world’s 2nd-largest chicken QSR, offering Louisiana-style Cajun fried chicken and chicken sandwiches. 3) Dunkin’: The company holds exclusive rights to develop and operate Dunkin' restaurants in India, the largest coffee and donut brand in the USA, serving coffee and baked goods. 4) Hong’s Kitchen: Hong’s Kitchen is the company’s first homegrown brand and India’s only Chinese QSR. 5) COFFY: Through the acquisition of DP Eurasia, the company has entered Turkey’s high-frequency coffee consumption market under the “COFFY” brand, which ranks as the 8th largest café brand in Turkey. [1] [2] [3]

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Jubilant FoodWorks (consolidated, continuing operations, Rs crore). FY26 (Mar-2026) is the base year. Two-part model: India (sales within India: Domino's, Popeyes, Hong's) and International (DP Eurasia, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh), each with revenue growth and EBITDA margin after Ind AS 116 (rent excluded, ESOP included). India revenue is built from Domino's stores x revenue per store plus the emerging brands (businessLines), checked in JUBLFOOD.ctx.js. Minorities (DP Eurasia ~6.35%, Bangladesh 49%) sit in the tax line for EPS and are deducted in the SOTP.

segments.name: India
segments._why: Sales within India +13.1% in FY26 (Rs6,057 cr to Rs6,848 cr; Domino's +12.0% on 276 net new stores and LFL 6.5%); Q1FY27 standalone +9.2% (Domino's +7.4%, LFL 2.5%, orders +6.5%; Popeyes +97%). Built from Domino's stores (230-250 openings guided for FY27) x revenue per average store, which falls in FY27 as LFL stays below the 5-7% medium-term guide and new stores split old catchments, plus Popeyes and Hong's at +65% / +45% / +35% (businessLines).
segments._marginWhy: Standalone EBITDA margin 19.7% (FY25), 20.0% (FY26), 19.5% in Q1FY27 (19.3% a year earlier) after ~200 bp of cost inflation (LPG, minimum wages, Labour Codes) was cut to ~20 bp by pricing and productivity. Management keeps a +200 bp pre-Ind AS target (emerging-brand drag ~200 bp to ~100 bp by end-FY28, ~100 bp from Domino's). We assume 20.2% / 20.8% / 21.3%: ~+125 bp over three years, below guidance because the Rs99 minimum order value and dine-in weakness cost margin.

segments.name: International
segments._why: Sales outside India +30.1% in FY26 (DP Eurasia +28.8% in rupees, Sri Lanka +64%, Bangladesh +27%); Q1FY27 DP Eurasia +28.2%. Rupee growth is mostly Turkish inflation less lira depreciation: Domino's Turkey LFL +30.6% in lira but -1.3% after inflation. We assume +22% / +15% / +13% as Turkish inflation eases, with ~60 net new stores a year.
segments._marginWhy: 19.1% (FY25), 19.3% (FY26); Q1FY27 20.0% vs 20.5% a year earlier as the IAS 29 monetary gain shrank (ex-MGL margin +15 bp). We assume 18.8% / 19.0% / 19.2%: a smaller monetary gain as inflation falls, offset by operating leverage; DP Eurasia PAT margin guided at 7-9% for FY27.

assumptions._unallocWhy: International EBITDA is defined as consolidated less standalone, so the two parts add to the company's EBITDA by construction.
assumptions._esopWhy: Share-based payment (Rs28.8 cr in FY26, AR cash flow) is already inside segment EBITDA; the array is kept at zero for the Excel model.

businessLines._why: India revenue = Domino's India (average stores x revenue per average store) + emerging brands (Popeyes, Hong's). FY26: Domino's Rs6,629.4 cr on 2,317 average stores (2,179 to 2,455) = Rs2.861 cr per store (FY25 Rs2.835 cr on 2,087 average stores, 1,995 to 2,179); emerging brands Rs218.7 cr (sales within India less Domino's). Revenue per average store +0.9% in FY26 with LFL 6.5%: new and split stores dilute it by ~5-6 points. We assume -2.0% / +0.5% / +1.0% with LFL ~4.5% / ~6% / ~6%.

assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex plus lease principal, because reported EBITDA excludes rent (LENSKART/ETERNAL treatment). Cash capex (PPE and intangibles) Rs863 cr (FY25), Rs999 cr (FY26: India Rs803 cr, outside India Rs191 cr). Guidance Rs750-900 cr a year for India (stores, store upgrades, technology; supply chain past its peak after the Mumbai commissary). We assume India Rs850 / 875 / 900 cr and International Rs210 / 230 / 250 cr. Lease principal (lease payments less lease interest) ~Rs243 cr in FY25 and ~Rs303 cr in FY26; we assume Rs345 / 390 / 435 cr.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs959 cr = 8.8% of average gross block (Rs10,885 cr, Screener incl. right-of-use). Q1FY27 Rs255 cr (Rs1,020 cr annualised) with the Mumbai commissary in for a full quarter. 8.6% gives FY27E ~Rs1,070 cr; the engine never retires assets, so a rate a little below history keeps depreciation near 9.7% of revenue (10.1% in FY26).
assumptions._treasuryWhy: The model's net treasury is negative (borrowings Rs1,745 cr and lease liabilities Rs3,157 cr against Rs434 cr of cash and investments at Mar-2026), so no yield is applied; income on deposits is in the fixed other income.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Other income Rs73.7 cr (FY25) and Rs74.1 cr (FY26: interest on sub-lease receivables Rs39.2 cr, bank deposits Rs10.8 cr, security deposits Rs8.2 cr, mutual funds Rs5.6 cr, other Rs10.3 cr; AR note 25), plus the share of associates (Rs7.0 cr in FY26, Rs4.1 cr in Q1FY27), which the engine has no line for. Q1FY27: Rs18.7 cr + Rs4.1 cr = Rs22.8 cr (Rs91 cr annualised). We assume Rs85 / 90 / 95 cr.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs436 cr = lease interest Rs337 cr + interest on borrowings Rs99 cr (Rs217 cr in FY25, before DP Eurasia's lira loans were refinanced in euro); Q1FY27 Rs120 cr (Rs481 cr annualised). Lease interest grows ~9-10% with the store base; bank interest edges down as debt is repaid.
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax on continuing PBT before exceptional items ~27-28% in FY26 (India 25.17%, Turkey 25-30% plus dividend withholding tax). The engine has no minority line, so ~2.5-3 points are added for minorities' share of profit (Rs15.8 cr in FY26, ~Rs3 cr in Q1FY27). Q1FY27 attributable profit was 66% of PBT (34% combined), inflated by tax on Turkish dividends.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend Rs1.20 a share for FY25 and FY26 (Rs79 cr, ~18% of FY26 attributable profit).

dcf._betaWhy: Beta 0.9 gives 11.9%, which we use as the discount rate: it equals a WACC of ~11.9% with lease liabilities and bank debt at ~13% of enterprise value (cost of equity ~12.5%, after-tax cost of debt and leases ~7.5%). The engine discounts at one rate, so beta is set to land on the WACC (PLAYBOOK §7).
dcf._tgWhy: Eating out is under-penetrated in India (management: 6-7 million Indians eat pizza in a month); Turkey adds inflation-driven nominal growth. 5.5%, mid-range of the house 5-6%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~12% in FY29E to 8% by FY42E.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA (after Ind AS 116) edges from 20.6% (FY29E) to 21.5%: about half of the guided +200 bp, as rent, wages and aggregator-led price competition absorb part of the operating leverage.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex including lease principal fades from ~11.6% of revenue (FY29E) to 9% (cash capex ~6%, lease principal ~3%); depreciation incl. right-of-use 8.5% of revenue long run (10.1% in FY26).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Domino's LFL returns to the 5-7% guide from H2FY27 as dine-in recovers; Popeyes reaches Rs1,000 cr by FY29-30 and turns EBITDA-positive; the +200 bp pre-Ind AS margin target is met by FY28; Turkey keeps compounding with lower inflation.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: LFL stays near 0-3% as aggregators (Rs49-99 minimum orders) and rivals take share; new stores cannibalise old ones; LPG, cheese and wage inflation keep margins flat; a lira devaluation or a hyperinflation shock cuts rupee profit from Turkey.

Rs1.6 cr Dunkin) and principal ~Rs303 cr; FY25 Rs545.0 cr (interest Rs303.6 cr). Lease interest = finance cost less bank interest (Rs110 / 100 / 90 cr).

Holders: 6.35% of DP Eurasia and 49% of Jubilant Golden Harvest (Bangladesh). Applied to the equity value in the SOTP (INDHOTEL precedent). The put option on DP Eurasia minorities (Rs63 cr booked against equity) is the same claim and is not deducted again.

cover.headline: India's pizza leader is cheap against its own history: growth is slower, but the multiple has fallen further
cover.lead: Jubilant FoodWorks (JFL) runs Domino's in India (2,455 stores), Popeyes and Hong's Kitchen, and since Feb-2024 owns 93.65% of DP Eurasia (Domino's and COFFY in Turkey, Azerbaijan, Georgia). FY26 revenue rose 17.4% to ₹9,513 cr, but Domino's India like-for-like (LFL) growth fell from 11.6% to 0.2% during the year and was 2.5% in Q1FY27. We forecast EPS of ₹7.09 / ₹9.15 / ₹11.27 for FY27-29E, in line with consensus. The street values JFL on **EV/EBITDA after rent, India plus International (24-30x and 15-18x FY28E)**. The house rule (its own forward EV/EBITDA median since Apr-2021, 23.5x, times the QSR peers' −27.0% move against their five-year medians) gives **17x Sep-28E EBITDA of ₹2,648 cr, less minorities = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with BUY.** That is ≈23.0x EBITDA after rent on the street's basis, inside its range. Cross-checks: P/E ₹802, DCF ₹333. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The multiple has fallen more than the business
arguments.p: At ₹456.70 JFL trades at 13.4x Sep-28E EBITDA (after Ind AS 116, leases in debt), against a 23.5x one-year-forward median since Apr-2021 and 21.4x since Turkey was consolidated. Its trailing EV/EBITDA is −44.3% below its five-year median; Westlife, Devyani and Sapphire are a median −27.0% below theirs. EBITDA still grew ~19% in FY26 and 14% in Q1FY27.

arguments.h: Domino's India: orders are growing, ticket size is not
arguments.p: Q1FY27 orders +6.5%, delivery revenue +12.1%, but LFL only 2.5% as the ₹99 minimum order (matching aggregators) cut ticket sizes and dine-in kept shrinking. We assume LFL of ~4.5% in FY27E against the 5-7% guide and ~240-260 new stores a year: India revenue +{{as.segments.0.growth.0|pct0}} / +{{as.segments.0.growth.1|pct0}} / +{{as.segments.0.growth.2|pct0}}.

arguments.h: Popeyes and the supply chain are the operating leverage
arguments.p: Popeyes grew revenue 97% in Q1FY27 with LFL above 40% for a third quarter; management targets a ₹1,000 cr brand in 3-4 years. Supply-chain capex is past its peak (capacity for ~5,000 stores), so capex stays ~₹750-900 cr while revenue grows. Management keeps a +200 bp after-rent margin goal by FY28; we model about +125 bp over three years.

arguments.h: Turkey: real growth hidden by inflation accounting
arguments.p: DP Eurasia (₹2,456 cr revenue, ₹204 cr PAT in FY26) grows ~28% in rupees, but Domino's Turkey LFL was −1.3% after inflation in Q1FY27 and reported EBITDA swings with the IAS 29 monetary gain. It brings minorities (6.35%), most of the ₹1,745 cr bank debt (euro loans due in FY27) and currency risk; we value it at the group multiple and show a lower one as a sensitivity.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): management expects Domino's LFL above Q1's 2.5%; the base eases from Q3 (5.0%, then 0.2%).
Refinancing of the two euro term loans (EUR 109.6 mn, ~₹1,183 cr) that fall due in FY27.
Popeyes: 35-40 openings a year and the path to EBITDA break-even.
Dunkin' exit under way (27 stores at Mar-2026, 15 at Jun-2026): a cleaner standalone P&L from FY27.
Turkish inflation and the lira: a lower monetary gain cuts reported International EBITDA.

blocks.callout: **How it makes money:** JFL buys and processes its own ingredients in central commissaries, delivers through its own riders, and keeps a ~75% gross margin on Domino's India. Out of that it pays staff (~17% of revenue), royalties to Domino's Pizza Inc., rent (~7.5% of India revenue), marketing, energy and delivery costs. What is left is ~20% EBITDA before rent and ~12.6% after it in India. Scale is the business model: more stores in the same city lower the delivery time and the supply-chain cost per order.

sections.title: Indian QSR: a small, fast-growing category where aggregators now set the price of convenience

blocks.p: Chained quick-service restaurants (QSR) are a small slice of Indian food spending. JFL's FY26 presentation (citing industry reports) sizes India's chained QSR market at ~US$3.2 bn in 2024 growing to ~US$5.4 bn by 2028 (~14% a year), with chains at ~6% of a ~US$60 bn foodservice market (US ~US$800 bn, China ~US$760 bn). Delivery is the growth channel: food aggregators cut minimum order values to ₹99 and then ₹49, which pulled small, solo orders away from dine-in and takeaway and forced Domino's to match (₹149 to ₹99). Listed rivals: Westlife (McDonald's West & South), Devyani (KFC, Pizza Hut, Costa) and Sapphire (KFC, Pizza Hut) - both Yum franchisees - and Restaurant Brands Asia (Burger King India). KFC (Devyani, Sapphire) is the fried-chicken incumbent Popeyes is attacking. Most listed rivals made losses or near-zero profit in FY26 as same-store sales fell.

Domino's gained ~80 bp of delivery share among the top 25 QSR brands year on year in Q1FY27 (NielsenIQ, per the Q1FY27 letter); JFL calls itself the largest QSR player for 30 years, ~1.7x the second largest (FY26 presentation). DP Eurasia runs 787 Domino's stores in Turkey, Azerbaijan and Georgia and COFFY is the 5th largest coffee brand in Turkey by stores (194). Turkey has been hyperinflationary under IAS 29 since 2022; Domino's Turkey LFL was +30.6% in lira but -1.3% after inflation in Q1FY27.

blocks.p: Domino's India revenue grew 12% in FY26 to ₹6,629 cr on 276 net new stores (2,455 at Mar-2026) and LFL growth of 6.5% (simple average of the quarters: 11.6%, 9.1%, 5%, 0.2%). In Q1FY27 revenue grew 7.4% and LFL 2.5% on a high base (11.6%), with orders +6.5%, delivery revenue +12.1% (76.1% of revenue) and ~140 bp of net price increases. Two things hold LFL back: the ₹149→₹99 minimum order value cut lower tickets, and dine-in/takeaway (DITA) keeps losing small solo orders to ₹49-99 aggregator deliveries. Management has put a dedicated leader on DITA, is upgrading ~400 dine-in-heavy stores and says Q2 started better. Revenue per average store rose only 0.9% in FY26 (₹2.84 cr to ₹2.86 cr) despite 6.5% LFL: new and split stores dilute it.

blocks.p: Popeyes had 78 stores at Mar-2026 and 88 at Jun-2026 (+10 in Q1FY27). Same-store growth was 28% in FY26 and above 40% for three quarters to Q1FY27; revenue grew 97% in Q1FY27 and system average daily sales passed ₹95,000 (seven cities above ₹1 lakh for the quarter), vs ~₹80,000 for a mature Domino's store. Management targets a ₹1,000 cr brand in three to four years with 35-40 openings a year (sites identified for the next 200) and says EBITDA profitability is "the next challenge": restaurant-level profits exist, but marketing and the team built for a ₹1,000 cr brand weigh on a business of a few hundred crore. Hong's Kitchen (29 stores) is not being funded further and Dunkin' has been exited. The drag of emerging brands on standalone after-rent EBITDA was ~220 bp in FY26 (~200 bp without Dunkin'), and management aims to bring it to ~100 bp by end-FY28.

blocks.p: Sales outside India rose from ₹2,047 cr (FY25) to ₹2,664 cr (FY26, +30.1%). DP Eurasia (93.65% owned) reported revenue of ₹2,456 cr (+28.8%) and PAT of ₹204 cr (8.3%), up 62% with lower interest after its lira loans were moved into euro; Q1FY27 revenue +28.2%. Reported EBITDA includes the IAS 29 monetary gain on net monetary liabilities, which fell in Q1FY27 as inflation eased: International EBITDA margin was 20.0% vs 20.5% a year earlier, but +15 bp excluding it. sections.title: Clean audit; four things to adjust for: rent outside EBITDA, Turkey's inflation accounting, one-offs and minorities

bullets: **EBITDA excludes rent.** Ind AS 116 moves rent into depreciation and interest (lease interest ₹337 cr in FY26) and the cash into financing (₹641 cr of lease payments). Operating cash flow (₹1,894 cr) therefore overstates cash earnings; we treat lease principal as capex in the forecasts and show EBITDA after rent separately.

**Hyperinflation (IAS 29).** DP Eurasia's results are restated to the latest Turkish price level each period, include a monetary gain or loss on net monetary items inside EBITDA, and are translated at the closing lira rate. Quarterly International margins and DP Eurasia's PAT are therefore noisy; management asks investors to judge them on a full year.

**One-offs.** FY24: ₹170 cr gain on remeasuring the old DP Eurasia stake. FY25: ₹4.5 cr associate write-down; Dunkin' and Russia losses (₹33 cr) in discontinued operations. FY26: ₹33.7 cr Labour Code charge; discontinued operations +₹58 cr (Russia gain ₹82 cr less Dunkin' ₹24 cr). EPS before these: ₹4.14 (FY24), ₹3.70 (FY25), ₹6.08 (FY26) vs reported ₹6.05, ₹3.19, ₹6.49. Our forecasts carry none of them; Screener's annual "other income" includes them, so its FY24 and FY26 profit look better than the business.

**Minorities.** ₹15.8 cr of FY26 profit (₹3 cr in Q1FY27) belongs to DP Eurasia's 6.35% outside holders and the Bangladesh partner; we use profit after minorities (JUBLFOOD.patch.js), add ~2.5-3 points to the tax rate in forecasts and deduct their share of value in the SOTP.

**Screener vs company EBITDA.** Screener's FY26 EBITDA (₹1,902 cr) is ₹14 cr above the company's (₹1,888 cr) because it shows losses on store discards below EBITDA; we forecast on the company basis. Screener's Q1-Q2FY26 quarters still include Dunkin'.
**Intangibles.** Goodwill ₹799 cr and other intangibles ₹1,355 cr (mostly DP Eurasia's brand and master-franchise rights, indefinite-life, tested yearly; no impairment in FY26).

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Deloitte Haskins & Sells gives a clean opinion and we found nothing improper. The amber reflects how much judgement sits between reported and underlying profit: hyperinflation restatement, two years of re-presented discontinued operations, and a headline EBITDA that leaves out the largest store cost.

blocks.p: The street uses a sum of the parts on EV/EBITDA after rent ("pre-Ind AS 116"): India at 24-30x FY28E/Jun-28E and International at 15-18x, or DP Eurasia on P/E. We use EV/EBITDA on the same horizon (Sep-28E: half FY28E, half FY29E), but on reported EBITDA before rent with lease liabilities (₹3,157 cr at Mar-2026) counted as debt, the basis on which the stock's own history can be measured. We apply one group multiple to India and International (the history has included Turkey since FY25) and deduct minorities (3.0% of equity value). On the street's basis our target equals **23.0x** Sep-28E after-rent EBITDA (₹1,813 cr), inside its 21-26x blended range. sections.title: Our honest summary: a slower but sound business at 13.4x Sep-28E EBITDA; BUY on valuation

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's largest QSR (2,455 Domino's stores, 76% delivery on its own app and fleet), a supply chain built for ~5,000 stores, Popeyes growing ~100%, and a cash-generating Turkish franchise (DP Eurasia, ₹204 cr PAT in FY26). Growth has slowed: Domino's LFL 2.5% in Q1FY27, revenue per store flat, margins ~20% before rent and ~13% after it.

**What you are paying:** ₹456.70 is 13.4x Sep-28E EBITDA (leases in debt), ≈17.5x after rent on the street's basis, and 49.9x FY28E EPS. Since Apr-2021 the stock has traded at a median 23.5x forward EBITDA; QSR peers trade ~27% below their five-year medians, JFL ~44% below its own. The rule gives 17x; the street median is ₹572.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Jubilant FoodWorks (consolidated, continuing operations, Rs crore). FY26 (Mar-2026) is the base year. Two-part model: India (sales within India: Domino's, Popeyes, Hong's) and International (DP Eurasia, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh), each with revenue growth and EBITDA margin after Ind AS 116 (rent excluded, ESOP included). India revenue is built from Domino's stores x revenue per store plus the emerging brands (businessLines), checked in JUBLFOOD.ctx.js. Minorities (DP Eurasia ~6.35%, Bangladesh 49%) sit in the tax line for EPS and are deducted in the SOTP.

segments.name: India
segments._why: Sales within India +13.1% in FY26 (Rs6,057 cr to Rs6,848 cr; Domino's +12.0% on 276 net new stores and LFL 6.5%); Q1FY27 standalone +9.2% (Domino's +7.4%, LFL 2.5%, orders +6.5%; Popeyes +97%). Built from Domino's stores (230-250 openings guided for FY27) x revenue per average store, which falls in FY27 as LFL stays below the 5-7% medium-term guide and new stores split old catchments, plus Popeyes and Hong's at +65% / +45% / +35% (businessLines).
segments._marginWhy: Standalone EBITDA margin 19.7% (FY25), 20.0% (FY26), 19.5% in Q1FY27 (19.3% a year earlier) after ~200 bp of cost inflation (LPG, minimum wages, Labour Codes) was cut to ~20 bp by pricing and productivity. Management keeps a +200 bp pre-Ind AS target (emerging-brand drag ~200 bp to ~100 bp by end-FY28, ~100 bp from Domino's). We assume 20.2% / 20.8% / 21.3%: ~+125 bp over three years, below guidance because the Rs99 minimum order value and dine-in weakness cost margin.

segments.name: International
segments._why: Sales outside India +30.1% in FY26 (DP Eurasia +28.8% in rupees, Sri Lanka +64%, Bangladesh +27%); Q1FY27 DP Eurasia +28.2%. Rupee growth is mostly Turkish inflation less lira depreciation: Domino's Turkey LFL +30.6% in lira but -1.3% after inflation. We assume +22% / +15% / +13% as Turkish inflation eases, with ~60 net new stores a year.
segments._marginWhy: 19.1% (FY25), 19.3% (FY26); Q1FY27 20.0% vs 20.5% a year earlier as the IAS 29 monetary gain shrank (ex-MGL margin +15 bp). We assume 18.8% / 19.0% / 19.2%: a smaller monetary gain as inflation falls, offset by operating leverage; DP Eurasia PAT margin guided at 7-9% for FY27.

assumptions._unallocWhy: International EBITDA is defined as consolidated less standalone, so the two parts add to the company's EBITDA by construction.
assumptions._esopWhy: Share-based payment (Rs28.8 cr in FY26, AR cash flow) is already inside segment EBITDA; the array is kept at zero for the Excel model.

businessLines._why: India revenue = Domino's India (average stores x revenue per average store) + emerging brands (Popeyes, Hong's). FY26: Domino's Rs6,629.4 cr on 2,317 average stores (2,179 to 2,455) = Rs2.861 cr per store (FY25 Rs2.835 cr on 2,087 average stores, 1,995 to 2,179); emerging brands Rs218.7 cr (sales within India less Domino's). Revenue per average store +0.9% in FY26 with LFL 6.5%: new and split stores dilute it by ~5-6 points. We assume -2.0% / +0.5% / +1.0% with LFL ~4.5% / ~6% / ~6%.

assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex plus lease principal, because reported EBITDA excludes rent (LENSKART/ETERNAL treatment). Cash capex (PPE and intangibles) Rs863 cr (FY25), Rs999 cr (FY26: India Rs803 cr, outside India Rs191 cr). Guidance Rs750-900 cr a year for India (stores, store upgrades, technology; supply chain past its peak after the Mumbai commissary). We assume India Rs850 / 875 / 900 cr and International Rs210 / 230 / 250 cr. Lease principal (lease payments less lease interest) ~Rs243 cr in FY25 and ~Rs303 cr in FY26; we assume Rs345 / 390 / 435 cr.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs959 cr = 8.8% of average gross block (Rs10,885 cr, Screener incl. right-of-use). Q1FY27 Rs255 cr (Rs1,020 cr annualised) with the Mumbai commissary in for a full quarter. 8.6% gives FY27E ~Rs1,070 cr; the engine never retires assets, so a rate a little below history keeps depreciation near 9.7% of revenue (10.1% in FY26).
assumptions._treasuryWhy: The model's net treasury is negative (borrowings Rs1,745 cr and lease liabilities Rs3,157 cr against Rs434 cr of cash and investments at Mar-2026), so no yield is applied; income on deposits is in the fixed other income.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Other income Rs73.7 cr (FY25) and Rs74.1 cr (FY26: interest on sub-lease receivables Rs39.2 cr, bank deposits Rs10.8 cr, security deposits Rs8.2 cr, mutual funds Rs5.6 cr, other Rs10.3 cr; AR note 25), plus the share of associates (Rs7.0 cr in FY26, Rs4.1 cr in Q1FY27), which the engine has no line for. Q1FY27: Rs18.7 cr + Rs4.1 cr = Rs22.8 cr (Rs91 cr annualised). We assume Rs85 / 90 / 95 cr.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs436 cr = lease interest Rs337 cr + interest on borrowings Rs99 cr (Rs217 cr in FY25, before DP Eurasia's lira loans were refinanced in euro); Q1FY27 Rs120 cr (Rs481 cr annualised). Lease interest grows ~9-10% with the store base; bank interest edges down as debt is repaid.
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax on continuing PBT before exceptional items ~27-28% in FY26 (India 25.17%, Turkey 25-30% plus dividend withholding tax). The engine has no minority line, so ~2.5-3 points are added for minorities' share of profit (Rs15.8 cr in FY26, ~Rs3 cr in Q1FY27). Q1FY27 attributable profit was 66% of PBT (34% combined), inflated by tax on Turkish dividends.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend Rs1.20 a share for FY25 and FY26 (Rs79 cr, ~18% of FY26 attributable profit).

dcf._betaWhy: Beta 0.9 gives 11.9%, which we use as the discount rate: it equals a WACC of ~11.9% with lease liabilities and bank debt at ~13% of enterprise value (cost of equity ~12.5%, after-tax cost of debt and leases ~7.5%). The engine discounts at one rate, so beta is set to land on the WACC (PLAYBOOK §7).
dcf._tgWhy: Eating out is under-penetrated in India (management: 6-7 million Indians eat pizza in a month); Turkey adds inflation-driven nominal growth. 5.5%, mid-range of the house 5-6%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~12% in FY29E to 8% by FY42E.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA (after Ind AS 116) edges from 20.6% (FY29E) to 21.5%: about half of the guided +200 bp, as rent, wages and aggregator-led price competition absorb part of the operating leverage.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex including lease principal fades from ~11.6% of revenue (FY29E) to 9% (cash capex ~6%, lease principal ~3%); depreciation incl. right-of-use 8.5% of revenue long run (10.1% in FY26).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Domino's LFL returns to the 5-7% guide from H2FY27 as dine-in recovers; Popeyes reaches Rs1,000 cr by FY29-30 and turns EBITDA-positive; the +200 bp pre-Ind AS margin target is met by FY28; Turkey keeps compounding with lower inflation.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: LFL stays near 0-3% as aggregators (Rs49-99 minimum orders) and rivals take share; new stores cannibalise old ones; LPG, cheese and wage inflation keep margins flat; a lira devaluation or a hyperinflation shock cuts rupee profit from Turkey.

Rs1.6 cr Dunkin) and principal ~Rs303 cr; FY25 Rs545.0 cr (interest Rs303.6 cr). Lease interest = finance cost less bank interest (Rs110 / 100 / 90 cr).

minorities._why: Minorities' share of profit: Rs3.0 cr of Rs100.0 cr in Q1FY27 (3.0%); FY26 Rs15.8 cr of Rs444.2 cr (3.6%), incl. ~Rs5 cr share of the Russia sale gain (Russia sat under DP Eurasia), ~2.7% excluding it. Holders: 6.35% of DP Eurasia and 49% of Jubilant Golden Harvest (Bangladesh). Applied to the equity value in the SOTP (INDHOTEL precedent).
